newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-WOODS MAKES RYDER CUP CHECK ON VALDERRAMA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS MAKES RYDER CUP CHECK ON VALDERRAMA.

text.p: Tiger Woods joined his prospective U.S. Ryder Cup team mates at the Spanish venue for September's clash with Europe on Sunday and admitted the course was trickier than he had imagined.

The U.S. Masters champion was whisked straight from the airport to the Valderrama Ryder Cup course where he met team captain Tom Kite and accompanied Mark O'Meara, Payne Stewart and David Duval in a practice round.
"The course requires a lot of strategy," said Woods. "It surprised me, there are more dog-legs than I thought and trees overhanging.
"I'll be hitting a lot of two-irons here. In September I expect Valderrama to be dry and hard so the ball will run.
"I think the guys that didn't come missed out."

Three of Kite's original party did not appear, including Tom Lehman, winner of the Loch Lomond Invitational on Saturday, who defends his British Open title at Royal Troon this week. Steve Jones and Tommy Tolles also pulled out of the inspection at the last minute.
Woods, expected to be among Lehman's main challengers in Scotland, identified the Seve Ballesteros-designed par five 17th as a crucial hole. "If it gets firm that hole could be scary."
Davis Love III and Corey Pavin agreed with their compatriot's assessment.

"It's a make or break hole," said Love. "With five holes to play you'll be thinking about 17 where you'll have a chance to turn the match your way with a birdie or lose with a bogey. It's a great match play hole."
Stewart, who says he needs to win a tournament to make the U.S. team, was not overawed by the Sotogrande course.
"I was talking to Jose Maria Olazabal last week and he told me Valderrama was pretty straightforward and he's right," said Stewart.
"As long as you hit the ball in the right place you're okay. I'm happy."
Kite will announce his captain's choices for the September 26-28 match following the U.S. PGA championship next month.
